nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiMoO4 growth
nodes.procedure: NiMoO4 precursor was first grown on commercial Ni foam using a simple hydrothermal method.
nodes.source_text: The synthetic process of the Fe/MoNi4/MoO2 nanoarray is described in the schematic illustration (Fig. 1a). In brief, a NiMoO4 precursor was first grown on commercial Ni foam using a simple hydrothermal method.

nodes.name: Ar annealing of NiMoO4
nodes.procedure: the NiMoO4 precursor was directly treated in an Ar atmosphere at 400 °C
nodes.source_text: the NiMoO4 precursor was directly treated in an Ar and H2/Ar atmosphere at 400 °C, and the as-obtained samples are abbreviated as Δtr–NiMoO4 and MoNi4/MoO2

nodes.name: H2/Ar reduction of NiMoO4
nodes.procedure: the NiMoO4 precursor was annealed in an H2/Ar atmosphere at 400 °C to obtain MoNi4/MoO2
nodes.source_text: the NiMoO4 precursor was annealed in an H2/Ar atmosphere at 400 °C to obtain the final Fe/MoNi4/MoO2 hybrid nanorod array. During the heat treatment process, the NiMoO4 precursor was converted to MoNi4 and MoO2

nodes.name: Fe modification and H2/Ar reduction
nodes.procedure: After ferric nitrate modification, the NiMoO4 precursor was annealed in an H2/Ar atmosphere at 400 °C to obtain the final Fe/MoNi4/MoO2 hybrid nanorod array. During the heat treatment process, the NiMoO4 precursor was converted to MoNi4 and MoO2 accompanied by the formation of Fe nanoparticles through hydrogen reduction at high temperature.
nodes.source_text: After ferric nitrate modification, the NiMoO4 precursor was annealed in an H2/Ar atmosphere at 400 °C to obtain the final Fe/MoNi4/MoO2 hybrid nanorod array.

unit_operations.name: H2/Ar annealing/reduction
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the NiMoO4 precursor was annealed in an H2/Ar atmosphere at 400 °C

nodes.source_text: Fe/MoNi₄/MoO₂ hybrid generates a current density of 100 mA cm⁻² at an ultralow overpotential of 23 mV... extremely low overpotentials of 59, 92 and 135 mV to deliver 500, 1000 and 2000 mA cm⁻²... maintain its extraordinary catalytic activity at 500/1000 mA cm⁻² with a minor fluctuation of 17/23 mV after 100-hour testing

demands relatively low overpotentials of 277 and 297 mV to achieve high current densities of 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻²... negligible potential fluctuation according to steady chronopotentiometric tests at 50 and 500 mA cm⁻² for over 100 h

nodes.description: Overall water splitting performance in 1 M KOH symmetric two-electrode cell
nodes.source_text: requiring remarkably low cell voltages of 1.508 and 1.586 V to afford 100 and 500 mA cm⁻²... at 1000 mA cm⁻² with a remarkably low cell voltage of 1.638 V... 1.708 V to reach 2000 mA cm⁻²... minimal voltage fluctuation of 35 mV... for over 200 h... voltage increase of 34 mV... over 60 h at 2000 mA cm⁻²... faradaic efficiency (>98%)

nodes.description: HER benchmark performance in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: At 0.1 V, Fe/MoNi₄/MoO₂ achieves a current density of up to 1200 mA cm⁻², which is 14-fold higher than the noble Pt/C catalyst supported on Ni foam

nodes.description: OER benchmark performance in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: prominently superior to MoNi₄/MoO₂, MoO₂, Ar-NiMoO₄ and IrO₂ catalysts

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show Fe/MoNi₄/MoO₂ nanoarray with rod-like nanostructure and tiny Fe nanoparticles uniformly anchoring on MoNi₄/MoO₂ nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Typical scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images (Fig. S1, ESI†) show that the as-obtained NiMoO₄ samples display rod-like nanostructure arrays... plenty of tiny Fe nanoparticles can be observed uniformly anchoring on the MoNi₄/MoO₂ nanorods.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals MoNi₄/MoO₂ nanorods decorated with 10-20 nm metallic Fe nanoparticles; HRTEM shows lattice fringes of 0.202 nm (Fe(110)), 0.206 nm (MoNi₄(211)), 0.175 nm (MoNi₄(002)), and 0.244 nm (MoO₂(111)).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images were recorded on a single Fe/MoNi₄/MoO₂ nanorod, where the MoNi₄/MoO₂ nanorod decorated with numerous metallic Fe nanoparticles in the range of 10-20 nm is displayed... lattice fringes with the d-spacings of 0.202 and 0.206 nm, which correspond to the (110) planes of metallic Fe and the (211) planes of MoNi₄ crystals.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms elemental composition of Fe:Mo:Ni:O = 1:2:3:4 in Fe/MoNi₄/MoO₂ and uniform spatial elemental distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) analysis (Fig. S4, ESI†) further confirms that the final samples are composed of Fe, Mo, Ni and O elements with a molar ratio of 1:2:3:4.

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD of Fe/MoNi₄/MoO₂ shows strongest peak at 44.1° (MoNi₄(211)) and weak peak at 37° (MoO₂); no detectable Fe peaks due to low content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Typical XRD patterns of the powders (Fig. 2a) clearly reveal the strongest peak at 44.1° related to the (211) plane of MoNi₄ (JCPDS No. 03-1036), while the weak XRD signal at 37° can be attributed to the presence of MoO₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS shows Ni 2p with metallic Ni and oxidized Ni; Fe 2p₃/₂ peaks at 707.48 eV (metallic Fe) and 711.44 eV (Fe–O); Mo 3d with metallic Mo (228.31/231.46 eV), MoO₂ (229.28/232.43 eV), Mo⁵⁺ (230.53/233.68 eV), Mo⁶⁺ (232.47/235.62 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p XPS spectra (Fig. 2b) contain two pairs of spin–orbit peaks, which can be indexed to the formation of metallic Ni and oxidized species... Fe 2p core-level spectrum (Fig. 2c), which can be divided into two main 2p₃/₂ peaks at 707.48 and 711.44 eV... high-resolution spectrum of Mo 3d can be deconvoluted into four doublets corresponding to the metallic Mo (228.31 and 231.46 eV), MoO₂ (229.28 and 232.43 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge XANES shows Fe valence close to zero in Fe/MoNi₄/MoO₂, similar to Fe foil standard.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the Fe K-edge XANES spectra (Fig. 2e), the near-edge energy adsorption curve of Fe/MoNi₄/MoO₂ is similar to that of the standard Fe simple substance, suggesting that the Fe valence is closer to zero.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge EXAFS shows Fe–Fe bond length same as Fe foil, confirming no chemical interactions between Fe particles and MoNi₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, the Fourier transform (FT) k²-weighted EXAFS spectra (Fig. 2f) of Fe/MoNi₄/MoO₂ exhibit nearly the same Fe–Fe bond length as that of the Fe foil standard sample, further confirming no chemical interactions between Fe particles and MoNi₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during OER shows MoO₂ peaks (316, 893 cm⁻¹) disappearing at 1.72 V due to Mo dissolution; Ni-O peaks emerge at 466, 530 cm⁻¹ (1.47 V) shifting to 468, 545 cm⁻¹ (NiOOH at 1.52 V) with blue shifts indicating Fe³⁺ incorporation into NiOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectroscopy was utilized to monitor the real-time structure evolution of Fe/MoNi₄/MoO₂ during the OER process (Fig. 4e)... two new Raman peaks clearly appear at 466 and 530 cm⁻¹... which are attributed to the well-defined δ(Ni–O) and ν(Ni–O) vibration modes of NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ XPS during OER shows Fe⁰ disappearing and Fe–O shifting +0.2 eV at 1.42 V, then to 711.5 eV (oxyhydroxide) at 1.52 V; Ni transforms to NiOOH; Ni 2p₃/₂ shifts -0.3 eV (1.52-1.72 V) indicating Fe incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Fe 2p XPS spectra (Fig. 4g) collected at 1.12 V are still divided into three doublets... Once the anodic potential is tuned from 1.12 V to 1.42 V, the Fe⁰ signal gradually decreases and disappears, while the Fe–O signal shows a prominent positive shift of 0.2 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at various scan rates yields Cdl = 2.145 F cm⁻² for Fe/MoNi₄/MoO₂, highest among tested catalysts, indicating largest ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We measured the double-layer capacitance (Cdl) of the reference catalysts using an electrochemical method (Fig. S9, ESI†). It is noteworthy that Fe/MoNi₄/MoO₂ has the largest Cdl value (2.145 F cm⁻²) among all the investigated catalysts.
